component.name: PairDesk
component.summary: Use another computer's desktop with your USB devices

description.p: PairDesk lets you use another Linux computer on your network as if you were sitting at it: its full desktop with sound, microphone and clipboard, plus your own USB devices and folders.

ul.li: Use a security key (such as a YubiKey), webcam or USB drive plugged into the computer you sit at on the remote computer, or the other way round
Pairing with a one-time code: no passwords sent, nobody in between can take part
Its own encrypted connection on its own port, open only while remote access is on
Reconnects by itself after a Wi-Fi drop and puts devices and folders back
Finds computers on your network; a plain IP address is enough
Sets up the other computer over SSH if needed, even without its screen
Add-ons are installed only when first needed, after explaining what they are for, and removed cleanly

description.p: PairDesk is a KnowReva project.

screenshot.caption: The other computer's desktop, with PairDesk's toolbar
Connect to a paired computer and choose USB devices to share

description.p: Keyboard shortcuts such as Alt+Tab stay in the remote desktop; Right Ctrl or the keyboard button gives the keyboard back.
Signing in at the screen of a connected computer works again; pairing with a reinstalled computer asks to trust its new identity.
The sign-out notice respects Cancel and says so on the connecting computer.
Fixed signing out the other computer's session from its notice.
Pairing uses a new random key for every attempt, with nothing shared between installs. Pairing codes are hidden until you press Show.
Fixes the sent camera; sound devices can be chosen in Options.
Choose where the remote sound plays and which microphone is sent. The sent camera works in all camera apps.
The Camera menu can take back a camera lent as a USB device and send it as video.
The remote desktop opens in PairDesk's window with a toolbar for USB devices, camera, folders and full screen. Cameras are sent as smooth video and show up as a normal camera on the other computer.
Devices sent from another computer work in remote desktop sessions.
Fixes for the update window and for upgrading with USB sharing set up.
Fixed a repeating USB error.
USB setup from a terminal shows its progress and works with sudo-rs.
Remote access no longer switches the desktop server off; add-ons install over SSH.
Updates install on Ubuntu 26.04; missing add-ons on the other computer are installed over SSH.
Updates are offered before signing in to the other computer. Fixed a crash when disconnecting.
Fixed connecting while an earlier connection to the same computer was still open.
Paired computers are remembered by IP address and found again when it changes.
Fixed a wrong "signed in on the screen" message with GNOME Remote Login.
Paired computers update each other: whichever has the older PairDesk is offered the newer one. GNOME on Wayland (Ubuntu 25.10 and later) works through GNOME Remote Login.
New colours and icon.
Add a remote computer is a wizard: it finds computers on your network, works with a plain IP address, can set up the other computer over SSH and fetch the pairing code over SSH.
New name: PairDesk (was DeskBridge). Upgrading keeps settings and pairings.
Welcome screen, a self-check that explains how to fix problems, a new icon and store-ready packaging.
Clearer next steps after pairing over SSH.
